acceptance: 1) Entry: contact a person on /contact -> chat window. Data sources: GET /api/chat/conversations/[id] and POST messages/read. Poll normally every 3s while visible, never while hidden, and catch up immediately on return. Allow one request in flight; slow/failing requests back off 1/2/4/8/16/30s. Out-of-order/page-insert tests yield each ID once without seq regression. Read only the largest actually visible complete seq (E-76, E-77). 2) Cut off a response after the actual service persists a message. UI keeps confirmation-pending state and original UUID/body/email. Clicking chat-retry resends the original payload and returns the original receipt. Actual operator GET sees one message and the outbox contains one row. Before-persistence offline drafts remain tab-memory-only, without a refresh-recovery promise (E-18, E-37, E-38). 3) After cookie expiry/revocation or operator role revocation, the next poll and send are rejected by the server with no body or write. Changed threadId/seq/email cannot cross authorization. UI stops timers/old sends, preserves the current draft, and displays explicit new consultation; never silently change UUID or resend into another thread (E-78, E-85). Use the unique minimalist-flat style from section 11. At the actual service at 1920x1080, 1440x900, and 390x844, record GIFs and computed styles: 2px black borders, zero radius, no shadow, and accent #b45700. On each admin page, run D1-D6 and overflow probes with work/form/card and density7/gutter16/gap16/pad16. Labels and keyboard focus are reachable; touch-control targets measure at least 44px.

E-18.trigger: The same message is submitted repeatedly because of retries.
E-18.expect: Deduplicate by the client message identifier so the inbox contains one message and notifications are not triggered repeatedly.

E-37.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-37.trigger: Submission times out or the response is lost, leaving actual persistence unknown.
E-37.expect: Show a confirmation-pending or retryable state. Retry with the original client message identifier and return the original receipt result, without duplicating inbox or notification items.

E-38.scene: C-02 Offline messages and recovery from send failures
E-38.expect: Keep the message and optional email only in the current tab's memory. Allow retries and offer the existing contact-email entry point. Do not promise draft recovery after refresh, closure, or a crash, and do not write the draft to localStorage or logs.

E-76.trigger: The chat/inbox is visible and requests succeed.
E-76.expect: Use a normal interval of three seconds. Pause while the tab is hidden; when visible again, immediately catch up from the confirmed seq. Slow networks or repeated failures use bounded backoff up to 30 seconds. No round may accumulate unbounded in-flight requests.

E-77.trigger: There are multiple tabs, retries, out-of-order responses, or new messages inserted between pages.
E-77.expect: Merge and deduplicate by stable server seq and message identifier. Advance the cursor only through the fully received range. A late old response must not move the cursor backward, overwrite a newer reply, or skip messages on an omitted page.

E-78.trigger: A visitor session expires or is revoked, or an operator loses chat permission after previously holding ADMIN/SALES.
E-78.expect: Perform server-side authorization on the next poll and send, and stop returning conversation content. Changing threadId, seq, or email cannot read another consultation.

E-85.trigger: The cookie reaches seven idle days or 30 days since issuance, or is revoked.
E-85.expect: The server rejects access to the old conversation using that credential; the browser may start a new consultation. Re-entering the same email alone cannot restore the old conversation. Neither the cookie nor any frontend copy stores PII.
